chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Other trumpeters who impressed him: Buck Clayton and Charlie Shavers
summary: Buck Clayton impressed him in California, and he rates Charlie Shavers among the greatest all-around trumpet players.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Can you think of any of the other trumpet players along that line that we haven't -- do you remember them -- that impressed you, any of them?
Oh, so many of them impressed me.
When I first heard Buck Clayton he impressed me. When I first went to California he impressed me.
Gee whiz. And, of course, going back to the thirties, --

Oh, Charlie Shavers, I don't even talk about him. You put Charlie Shavers up there and then talk about the other trumpet players. That's the way I feel about him. He was fantastic. To me he was one of the greatest all-around trumpet players that ever lived. To me. That's my idea of him, you know. There's an album of (unintelligible) the genius of Charlie Shavers.
Si Oliver did the arrangements on that?
I played for him before (inaudible) & of here.
